blocks.title: Petrochemicals
blocks.text: Petrochemicals are compounds obtained mainly from crude oil and natural gas by refining and transformation.

Petrochemicals are used to make many everyday items in packaging, construction, textiles, electronics and medicine. Synthetic chemicals made from petrochemicals are their derivatives, and these are very important industrial products. Petrochemicals are changed into their derivatives by chemical reactions such as polymerisation, oxidation or substitution.

blocks.caption: Table 31.5 Derivatives of petrochemicals and their uses

blocks.prompt: What is the difference between a petrochemical and a chemical derived from it? Give an example.
blocks.explanation: A petrochemical is obtained directly from crude oil or natural gas (e.g. ethene); a derivative is made from it by a further reaction such as polymerisation (e.g. poly(ethene)).

items: Petrochemicals come from crude oil and natural gas.
Derivatives are made by polymerisation, oxidation or substitution (Table 31.5).
